message.content:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) systems have become central to scientific discovery, public policy, and everyday decision-making (including [the challenge of distinguishing {genuine generalization (from artifact memorization [and distributional shift {and deployment-specific risk}]})]). This paper examines how contemporary machine-learning systems can be evaluated under conditions of uncertainty, contested values, and evolving deployment contexts. We argue that technical metrics alone are insufficient; instead, a layered framework is needed that integrates statistical validation, interpretability analysis, and governance oversight. Our contribution is threefold: we develop a taxonomy of evaluation risk, propose a benchmark protocol combining adversarial testing and longitudinal monitoring, and discuss responsible AI practices that balance capability, autonomy, and human oversight.
